item.title: Dhaka-Chittagong rail services resume after 24 hours
item.description:
Train services on the Dhaka-bound line of the Dhaka-Chittagong route resumed at 12:50pm on Thursday, more than 24 hours after the Karnaphuli Commuter Express derailed in Comilla's Laksam.
The Bijoy Express, travelling from Chittagong to Mymensingh, was the first train to cross the accident site after the line reopened.
Omar Faruk Bhuiyan, station master of Laksam Railway Junction, said train services were now operating normally on both lines.
The damaged track was repaired by 7am on Thursday, but services remained suspended on the Dhaka-bound line because a derailed coach was found. During the suspension, trains in both directions used the other line, causing some disruption. The Chattala Express, bound for Dhaka, and the Paharika Express, bound for Sylhet, passed through Laksam at 10:23am and 10:48am, respectively, on Thursday.
The accident occurred around 12:30pm on Wednesday in the outer section of Naoti station, near Azgara Bazar in Laksam, when five coaches of the Karnaphuli Commuter Express and three wheels of its engine derailed. At least seven passengers were injured.
A rescue train from Chittagong reached the site on Wednesday evening. Recovery work was completed around 5am on Thursday, followed by track repairs.
Meanwhile, railway authorities suspended sub-assistant engineer Sarwar Alam over allegations that he failed to inform the control room about repair work underway at the accident site. He was responsible for the Feni region under the Eastern Railway’s engineering department.
A four-member committee has been formed to investigate the accident, Chittagong Divisional Railway Manager Mostafizur Rahman Bhuiyan said on Wednesday night.

item.title: 4,157 killed in nine months as nation marks Road Safety Day
item.description:
Twelve people died in a head-on collision in Natore on Tuesday. According to police and surviving passengers, the bus was being driven by its supervisor while the regular driver slept in the back.
Two days later, Bangladesh is observing National Road Safety Day with the familiar program of seminars, discussions and promises to make its roads safer.
The latest figures offer little reason for reassurance.
At least 4,157 people were killed and 5,391 injured in 4,285 road crashes between January and September this year, according to the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA). That is an average of more than 15 deaths every day.
This year’s observance, under the theme “Safe Roads, Prosperous Nation, Bangladesh First,” comes amid persistent concerns over unfit vehicles, unqualified drivers and the failure to enforce existing traffic laws.
The Natore crash brought several of those concerns into sharp focus.
Police and injured passengers said the RP Special Paribahan bus was heading towards Bonpara when its supervisor, Sohel Rana, took over the wheel after a stop at Ishwardi around 3am.
Ramjan Ali, a surviving passenger from Chapainawabganj, said the regular driver left his seat after the break. About an hour later, the bus collided with a truck, killing 12 people and injuring at least 25.
The circumstances of the crash have once again raised questions about who is allowed to drive passenger buses and how effectively transport operators are monitored.
The deaths in Natore are part of a much larger toll.
According to Bangladesh Jatri Kalyan Samity, at least 125,405 people were killed in 72,736 road crashes between 2013 and 2025. Another 176,249 people were left permanently disabled, the organisation said.
Children have been among the worst affected. Road Safety Foundation figures show that 7,963 children died in road crashes between January 2020 and September 2026.
Nearly 3,000 of them were killed in motorcycle crashes, while 2,812 died as pedestrians.
Yet the problems identified by successive governments and road safety experts remain largely unresolved.
BRTA records indicate that around 650,000 vehicles are operating without the required registration, route permits or fitness certificates. More than 75,000 buses and trucks have exceeded their prescribed economic lifespan.
The shortage of qualified professional drivers for heavy and medium vehicles is estimated at around 30%.
Vehicle fitness is another major concern. Around 70% of buses and minibuses in Dhaka and other major cities reportedly lack valid fitness documents.
Driver health also receives inadequate attention. At a BRTA and Dhaka Ahsania Mission health camp in 2023, around 73% of 541 drivers who underwent eye examinations were found to need glasses.
In 2019, the National Road Safety Council identified seven priority areas and made 111 recommendations to improve road safety.
Experts say there has been little visible progress in implementing them.
BUET Assistant Professor Kazi Md Saifun Newaz said the country already has the Road Transport Act 2018 and Road Transport Rules 2022, but legislation alone cannot prevent crashes.
“Everyone knows the causes of road crashes and their remedies. What is missing is consistent and coordinated action,” he said.
“Observing days will not solve anything.”
The BRTA says it has filed more than 110,000 cases through mobile courts and joint enforcement drives in the first nine months of this year, targeting unfit vehicles, invalid licences, speeding and other violations.
But the continuing death toll raises questions about whether these drives are producing lasting improvements.
Bangladesh Jatri Kalyan Samity Secretary General Mozammel Haque Chowdhury blamed institutional inefficiency, corruption and the influence of transport owners’ and workers’ groups for the persistent disorder.
Road Safety Foundation Executive Director Saidur Rahman said the dangers were particularly acute for children on rural roads, where vehicles frequently pass close to homes and enforcement is weak.
“The authorities know the causes and the consequences, but there is no remedy,” he said.
The government has pledged to enact a comprehensive road safety law by December 2027.
The proposed Road Safety Act 2026 includes free emergency treatment for crash victims, legal protection for people who assist the injured, a demerit-point system for traffic offenders and higher penalties for repeat violations.
Road Transport and Bridges Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam has also reaffirmed Bangladesh’s commitment to the UN target of halving road deaths and serious injuries by 2030.
For now, the country enters another Road Safety Day with thousands of lives lost, longstanding recommendations awaiting implementation and another deadly crash exposing the dangers on its highways.

item.title: Man beaten to death at Dhaka hospital over child theft suspicion
item.description:

The incident took place in front of the hospital’s children’s ward around 11pm on Wednesday. Police have detained a man in connection with the incident.
Police said Md Alam Sheikh was loitering in front of the children’s ward when relatives of children receiving treatment there became suspicious of him and questioned his presence at the hospital.
As he allegedly failed to provide a satisfactory explanation, several people dragged him downstairs and beat him, leaving him critically injured. He died early Thursday.
Police said they went to the scene after receiving an alert through the national emergency service 999. Alam’s identity was later confirmed through fingerprint verification.
He was from Natore. Police have contacted his family members, who are on their way to Dhaka.
Deputy Commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Tejgaon Division, Ibne Mizan said the body had been sent to the morgue of Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College for an autopsy.
He said one person had been detained in connection with the incident. He added that legal action will be taken if the victim’s family files a complaint with the police.

item.title: Shibir says youth detained over PM comment is not a member
item.description:
Islami Chhatra Shibir has denied that Abu Bakar Siddique, 22, detained over a Facebook comment about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s visit to Rajshahi, is a member of the organization.
Imran Nazir, president of the Rajshahi metropolitan unit of Islami Chhatra Shibir, said: “There is an attempt to put the blame on Shibir whenever something happens. But Abu Bakar Siddique is not one of our members.”
Abu Bakar was detained on Wednesday afternoon at his maternal uncle’s house in Gholharia village in Hatrāmchandrapur, Paba upazila, Rajshahi. His father, Ainal Haque, was also detained during the operation. Both are now in the custody of the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP).
Chandrima police station Officer-in-Charge Monirul Islam said police had found no information indicating whether Abu Bakar had previously been arrested or whether any case had been filed against him. His political affiliation was also unknown, he added.
Mahmud Hasan Limon, president of the Chhatra Dal unit at Rajshahi New Government Degree College, said: “I heard from people in the administration that Abu Bakar used to be involved with the Chhatra League. Now, apparently, he is involved with Chhatra Shibir. But I have not seen anything at the college. We did not really know him.”
Shariful Islam, an assistant professor in the History Department of Rajshahi New Government Degree College, said Abu Bakar was a regular student who had taken his first-year final examinations, although the results had not yet been published. He said he had not observed any misconduct by Abu Bakar at the college.
After learning about the Facebook comment, Shariful Islam spoke to several students. According to him, they said Abu Bakar’s father had previously supported the Awami League but had been associating with Jamaat-e-Islami since August 5.
Shariful Islam also said he had heard that Abu Bakar had been involved with the Bangladesh Chhatra League through his family, although he had not observed any such involvement at the college.
The Facebook comment appeared under a photograph of the prime minister posted by a page named “The Beauty of Rajshahi.” The account, bearing the name Abu Bakar Siddique, commented: “What a great opportunity. Only a sniper was missing.”
During his visit to Rajshahi on Tuesday, Tarique Rahman traveled on a Rajshahi University of Engineering and Technology (RUET) bus from the airport to Madrasa Maidan and then to Dharmasabha before returning to the airport. Large numbers of people lined both sides of the road to greet him, and he responded to their greetings.
Following the comment, law enforcement agencies launched an operation to identify the account holder.
According to local residents, a team from the Cyber Crime Unit of Rajshahi Metropolitan Police and Chandrima police station went to Abu Bakar’s house at around 2pm on Wednesday. He was not there, and his family members did not disclose his whereabouts.
At around 4pm, a team from SRB-5 arrived at the house in plain clothes. Unable to find Abu Bakar, the team detained his father for questioning. Ainal Haque subsequently told them that his son was staying at his maternal uncle’s house in Gholharia village.
SRB-5 members then took Ainal Haque to the house and detained Abu Bakar. A mobile phone used by the family was seized, and both were subsequently handed over to the DMP’s Detective Branch.
SRB-5 Commander Lieutenant Colonel Faisal Ishtiaq confirmed the handover, saying: “We have handed both of them over to the DB. They will provide further details about the matter later.”
Abu Bakar lives in the Kechuatail area under Chandrima police station in Rajshahi city. His father, a farmer, has 4 children, with Abu Bakar being the eldest.
On Thursday morning, Monirul Islam searched Abu Bakar’s house. After nearly an hour, police found no evidence worth seizing apart from the packaging of a pen drive.
Police also attempted to recover Abu Bakar’s laptop, but family members said he neither used nor owned one.

item.title: Six law enforcers injured as gunfire targets Sajek tourist convoy
item.description:
Six members of law enforcement agencies were injured in an attack on a tourist convoy amid a road blockade on the Sajek-Baghaihat road in Rangamati’s Baghaichhari upazila on Thursday morning.
The incident occurred in the Ujobaazar area, prompting the army and police to evacuate the tourists to safety.
Rangamati Superintendent of Police Muhammad Abdur Rakib disclosed the details at a press conference at his office around 2:00pm on Thursday.
He said the Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee and the Sajek Karbari Association had enforced a road blockade from October 11 to 15. The programme was suspended from October 16 to 21 for Durga Puja, with plans to resume it thereafter.
The blockade left 2,933 tourists stranded in Sajek, the SP said.
To ensure their safe return, a convoy of tourist vehicles left Sajek around 9:00am on Thursday under the security escort of the Bangladesh army and police.
When the convoy reached Ujobaazar around 10:00am, law enforcement personnel held talks with the protesters to facilitate the tourists’ safe passage. The protesters then hurled bricks and stones at the security personnel, injuring six members, Abdur Rakib said.
The protesters were subsequently removed from the road, allowing the convoy to proceed.
Based on intelligence reports, authorities later learned that an armed group affiliated with the United People’s Democratic Front (UPDF) had opened fire targeting the tourist convoy, the SP said.
Law enforcement personnel returned fire to protect the tourists and safeguard public property, he added.
Intermittent exchanges of gunfire between the armed group and law enforcement personnel continued even after the tourists had been moved to safety.
The gunfight lasted from around 11:00am to 1:00pm, after which the situation came under control, Abdur Rakib said.
Md Jasim Uddin, a Mahindra driver on the Sajek route, said they left Sajek around 9:00am under a security escort.
“They were stopped by protesters at Ujobaazar around 10:00am and remained stranded for about 40 minutes. Later, security personnel dispersed the protesters using batons, allowing us to continue,” he said.
He said they reached Khagrachhari around 12:40pm.
Rahul Chakma John, organising secretary of the Sajek Cottage and Resort Owners Association, said around 3,000 tourists had returned from Sajek to Khagrachhari.
On Wednesday, Sajek Karbari Association President Natun Joy Chakma and Sajek Gano Odhikar Rokkha Committee Convener Babudhan Chakma announced in a joint statement that an indefinite road blockade would resume from Thursday.
The organisations alleged that armed members of the Parbatya Chattagram Jana-Samhati Samiti (JSS-Santu Larma) were active in different parts of Sajek.
They also alleged that the armed members had threatened and intimidated local residents, forced some people to leave their homes and seized mobile phones from villagers.
As a result, ordinary Jum farmers were unable to tend to their gardens, the organisations claimed.
They said the blockade would continue until the alleged armed members were removed from the area and measures were taken to ensure the safety and security of local residents.
Natun Joy Chakma said talks were underway with law enforcement agencies but they would not withdraw the blockade unless their three demands were addressed.
He said the blockade had been suspended from October 16 to 21 in observance of Durga Puja.
However, he alleged that the administration did not hold any discussions with them during that period.
He said tourists staying in Sajek had also been given sufficient time to leave, prompting them to resume the blockade as announced.
The indefinite blockade on the Sajek Road was initially launched on October 11 and suspended from October 16 to 21 for Durga Puja. With the blockade resuming on Thursday, concerns have resurfaced over tourist movement and security in Sajek.
According to local accounts, while the Bangladesh Army was escorting around 3,000 stranded tourists to safety, armed members of the United People’s Democratic Front (UPDF), along with women participating in the blockade, allegedly hurled bricks and stones at the tourists in the Gongaram Bazar area of Sajek.
The incident occurred as the tourists were being escorted out of the area amid the ongoing blockade.

item.title: Fire at Rangpur Medical College Hospital injures 40 patients
item.description:
At least 40 patients and their relatives were injured while rushing to evacuate Rangpur Medical College Hospital after a fire broke out due to a short circuit on Thursday morning.
The fire originated from a switchboard near the administrative section of the hospital’s electrical control room on the ground floor around 6:15am.
Firefighters quickly brought the blaze under control, but the hospital remained without electricity for six hours, triggering panic among patients and their attendants.
The power outage disrupted medical services, forcing the suspension of emergency surgeries and other treatments. Although partial power was restored to several wards after prolonged efforts, the nephrology, cardiology, gynaecology and kidney dialysis wards remained without electricity.
According to patients, hospital authorities and fire service officials, panic spread throughout the hospital as patients and their relatives rushed to leave the building. Those staying in wards on the second to fifth floors hurried down the stairs, with many falling and sustaining injuries. At least 40 people were injured in falls during the rush to evacuate the hospital.
As of 4pm, the offices of the hospital director, cardiology department, pathology ward, dermatology and venereology ward, kidney dialysis ward and nephrology ward remained without electricity, leaving patients struggling in the intense heat.
During a visit to the hospital, patients described the chaos surrounding the evacuation.
Shafiul Alam, a kidney patient receiving treatment in the second-floor nephrology ward, was being carried downstairs when his two nephews fell and were injured. Shafiul was also hurt in the incident.
At least 15 patients in the ward were injured while rushing downstairs, with some reportedly trampled in the crowd.
Several infants were also injured as patients and their attendants rushed down the stairs from the third-floor gynaecology ward with newborns.
Mamtaz Begum, a patient in the gynaecology ward, said her baby girl was born five days ago. After hearing about the fire, she rushed downstairs with her newborn and was injured during the evacuation.
Many others used the emergency exit stairs to escape, with several sustaining injuries in the rush.
Deputy Director of Rangpur Medical College Hospital Dr Md Abdul Mokaddem said the fire was caused by a short circuit.
“Efforts are underway to restore electricity to all wards,” he said.

The Climate Watch to deploy eight journalists at COP31
item.description:
As global attention turns to the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, Bangladeshi news organization The Climate Watch is preparing to bring South Asia’s climate struggles, demands and stories to the international stage.
Officially launched on November 3, 2024, The Climate Watch will deploy 8 journalists from Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka to cover the UN climate summit, scheduled for November 9-20. The team comprises 5 full-time journalists and 3 regional contributors, marking the publication’s largest international reporting operation to date.
While financial pressures have forced several established Western news organizations to reduce specialized reporting, The Climate Watch is expanding cross-border collaboration and investing in environmental journalism.
Founded in 2022 by award-winning Bangladeshi environmental journalist Shamsuddin Illius, The Climate Watch has developed into a regional platform connecting approximately 100 climate and environmental journalists.
“We are striving to become a voice for South Asia in global climate negotiations. Our countries are among the most vulnerable to climate change, and it is essential that we tell our own stories rather than rely solely on others to tell them for us,” Executive Editor Md Ibrahim Khalilullah said.
At COP31, its journalists will examine climate finance, adaptation, loss and damage, energy transition, biodiversity, displacement and climate justice, linking diplomatic negotiations to the everyday experiences of vulnerable communities.
The publication is also exploring collaborations with Shakti Foundation, Young Power in Social Action (YPSA) and Change Initiative to strengthen its coverage.
The Climate Watch’s investigations have examined deforestation, industrial expansion, groundwater depletion and environmental governance. An investigation into forest destruction around Chittagong’s National Special Economic Zone documented biodiversity losses, with its findings subsequently cited in public-interest litigation.
Its reporting has received international references from The Guardian, The Diplomat, Mongabay, The New Humanitarian and Fiji Sun, alongside academic citations involving Columbia University’s Climate School and the National University of Singapore.
Through its Birds in Climate Crisis initiative, the publication is producing 100 short documentaries on threatened birds, habitat destruction and changing ecosystems.
The outlet also contributed to Dark Side of the Boom, an Earth Journalism Network-coordinated investigation involving 14 newsrooms across 11 countries that examined the environmental consequences of digital infrastructure.
The collaboration received a 2026 Covering Climate Now Journalism Award, a Society of Publishers in Asia (SOPA) environmental reporting award and a special citation associated with the Osborn Elliott Prize.
Having covered COP28, COP29, COP30 and Bonn’s SB64 negotiations, The Climate Watch is also preparing to report on biodiversity negotiations at COP17 in Armenia.
Alongside its reporting, the organization conducts journalist training and pre-COP fellowships with the Center for Participatory Research and Development.
For the relatively young newsroom operating from climate-vulnerable Bangladesh, the COP31 deployment represents an effort to shift South Asia’s position in the global climate conversation from a region whose suffering is frequently reported by others to one increasingly telling its own stories.

item.title: Son of Myanmar’s Suu Kyi says had first call in five years
item.description:
The son of Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi said he spoke Thursday to the detained former democratic leader for the first time in more than five years.
“Today, I was finally able to speak with my mother, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, after more than five years. Hearing her voice again means more than words can express,” Kim Aris said in a post on Facebook.
Suu Kyi is under house arrest in the capital, Naypyidaw, according to Myanmar authorities, where she has been sequestered since being unseated in a 2021 military coup.
AFP could not immediately reach Aris -- who lives in the United Kingdom -- and it was not clear how he spoke to his mother, who won the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize for efforts to bring democracy to Myanmar.
However, he posted images accompanying his Facebook post which appeared to show him standing outside the Myanmar embassy in London.
“I am deeply grateful to everyone who has stood by my mother and me. I believe your voices helped make this moment possible,” Aris wrote.
“But my mother is 81 and remains unjustly detained. One conversation is not regular family access.”
Myanmar’s military held Suu Kyi in almost total seclusion for five years following the February 2021 coup, which ended a tentative decade-long experiment with democracy.
But in recent months authorities have increasingly advertised the loosening of her detention and published photographs of her taking private meetings, as supporters have demanded “proof of life” of the octogenarian.
On Monday, authorities in Myanmar said she received a package from Britain’s King Charles III, including two books about soil and a “sealed diplomatic communication” from the monarch.
Buckingham Palace did not comment on the contents of the communication.
Myanmar authorities said Suu Kyi was moved from a prison in Naypyidaw to house arrest in April, and in August they published images of her meeting the nation’s Red Cross representative.
After ruling Myanmar as military chief for five years, Min Aung Hlaing -- who ousted Suu Kyi in the 2021 coup -- was earlier this year installed as civilian president.
Analysts describe the election putting him in elected office as a charade, and say he may be loosening restrictions on Suu Kyi in a bid to court international legitimacy.

item.title: Matthew McConaughey sparks 2028 presidential speculation with call for independent candidates
item.description:
Oscar-winning actor Matthew McConaughey has reignited speculation about a possible run for the US presidency in 2028 after releasing a six-minute video urging voters to give independent candidates a greater role in American politics.
Released on October 18, ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, the video encourages voters to take independent candidates seriously rather than dismiss them as protest candidates or spoilers. McConaughey, however, did not announce any plans to run for office or endorse a candidate or political party.
“Independent does not mean you’re middle of the road. Independent is the original road,” he said, presenting political independence as an alternative to the traditional Republican-Democratic divide.
According to The Telegraph, McConaughey also argued that independently elected representatives could encourage compromise in a closely divided Congress and hold both major parties accountable. He urged voters to examine candidates’ positions and determine whether their views aligned with their own beliefs.
The video has prompted renewed discussion about the actor’s political ambitions, although McConaughey has neither confirmed nor ruled out a presidential bid.
His potential entry into politics has been a subject of speculation for several years. In 2021, he considered running for governor of Texas but ultimately decided against entering the race. In July 2024, he described himself as being on a “learning tour” while exploring the possibility of public office. He later said he would not pursue a political campaign at that time.
McConaughey’s latest remarks have also attracted criticism from commentators and social media users who questioned whether independent candidates could split the vote and influence closely contested elections.
The discussion comes amid growing identification with political independence in the United States. According to Gallup, 45% of Americans identified as political independents in 2025, a record high at the time.
For now, McConaughey’s video has renewed questions about his political future, but the actor has yet to announce any plans to enter the 2028 presidential race.

item.title: Gazipur’s ‘Ulka cinema hall’ to shut down in November
item.description:
Ulka, a long-running single-screen cinema hall at Gazipur Chowrasta, is set to close permanently in November as falling attendance, mounting losses and rising operating costs make it increasingly difficult to keep the business afloat.
Mohammad Rafiq Uddin, managing director of the cinema hall, confirmed the decision, saying ticket sales from current releases are no longer sufficient to cover even electricity bills.
“The hall is struggling to survive. We are incurring losses continuously. The films currently screening cannot even cover the electricity bill,” he said.
Rafiq Uddin said films with compelling stories and established stars continue to attract audiences. However, relying on releases concentrated around the two Eid festivals is not enough to sustain a cinema hall throughout the year.
He pointed to the audience response to films starring Shakib Khan, suggesting that more releases featuring the actor outside the Eid seasons could help single-screen cinemas remain viable.
Unusually high electricity bills have added to the financial strain, according to Rafiq Uddin. With operating expenses becoming increasingly difficult to manage, the owners have decided to shut down rather than continue accumulating losses.
Audience numbers have also declined sharply, hall authorities said. Some screenings attract only a handful of moviegoers, leaving ticket revenue insufficient to cover staff salaries and routine operating expenses.
The planned closure comes as Kamruzzaman’s Sneher Bondhon is screening at the venue. Starring Joy Chowdhury and Mou Khan, the film was released in 14 cinemas on October 16.
Its promotional campaign included appearances on an open-roof bus in Dhaka. However, reports from the exhibition circuit indicate that the film has struggled to attract audiences.
The closure will further narrow cinema-going options in Gazipur, an industrial district with a large working population. Local industry sources said four cinemas were operating in the district around a year to 18 months ago.
Once Ulka closes, only Barsha and Jhumur cinemas are expected to remain open in the district. Both venues are reportedly facing financial difficulties, raising further concerns about the future of single-screen cinema in the area.
Ulka’s shutdown highlights the challenges facing traditional cinema halls in Bangladesh, where declining attendance and rising operating costs continue to put pressure on venues that have long provided relatively affordable big-screen entertainment.

item.title: Chiranjit Biswas wins ‘Best Male Actor’ at Tasveer Film Festival

item.title: Jubo Dal leader hacked to death in Narayanganj
item.description:
A Jubo Dal leader was hacked to death in Sonargaon upazila of Narayanganj on Wednesday night.
The incident took place in the Char Kishoreganj area around 10pm, said Sonargaon police station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Abdul Barek.
The deceased, Fakir Zahir Rahman, 40, was the son of Abdur Rahman of Kalapaharia union in neighbouring Araihazar upazila. He was a joint convener of the upazila Jubo Dal and president of the union unit of the organization.
The OC told the media that although Zahir was originally from Araihazar, he had been living in a rented house in Munshiganj Sadar for several years. He also owned a pharmacy in Char Kishoreganj.
Citing preliminary findings, the OC said: “As he did every day, he was returning home after closing his pharmacy on Wednesday night. On the way, unidentified assailants hacked him with sharp weapons and left him injured on the road.”
Local residents later rescued him and took him to Munshiganj General Hospital, where he died while undergoing treatment.
The police official said the body was recovered and sent to the morgue of Narayanganj General Hospital for an autopsy.
The identities of those involved and the motive behind the killing were not immediately known. Police are investigating the incident, the OC added.

item.title: Bangladesh improves in rule of law index but trails several African nations
item.description:
Bangladesh has made a slight improvement in its overall rule of law score but continues to rank below several African countries, including Kenya, Zimbabwe and Nigeria, according to the Rule of Law Index 2026 released on Wednesday.
Bangladesh ranked 123rd among 143 countries and jurisdictions in the World Justice Project (WJP) index, behind Zimbabwe (122nd), Nigeria (120th), Sierra Leone (110th), Liberia (103rd), Kenya (100th) and Ghana (62nd).
Its score increased by 0.6% to 0.393 out of 1, up from 0.391 in 2025, making Bangladesh the world's 15th-biggest improver and South Asia's top gainer. Its ranking improved by two places from 125th, although its score remained below the global average of 0.55.
The index assesses countries across eight factors: constraints on government powers, absence of corruption, open government, fundamental rights, order and security, regulatory enforcement, civil justice and criminal justice.
Bangladesh improved in only three factors — constraints on government powers, absence of corruption and regulatory enforcement — while its performance declined in the other five.
Fundamental rights remained the country's weakest area, with Bangladesh ranking 133rd and scoring 0.30, placing it among the 11 lowest-ranked countries.
The indicator assesses the protection of fundamental human rights under international law. Civil justice was the second-weakest area, with Bangladesh ranking 132nd and scoring 0.36. The indicator measures access to and the effectiveness of the civil justice system in resolving grievances.
Bangladesh ranked 124th in regulatory enforcement, with a score of 0.40, and 117th in criminal justice, scoring 0.32. In the absence of corruption category, which measures bribery, improper influence and the misappropriation of public resources, it ranked 113th with a score of 0.35.
The country ranked 111th in constraints on government powers, which measures accountability under the law, with a score of 0.38.
Open government was Bangladesh's highest-ranked factor at 106th, with a score of 0.41. It assesses government transparency, accountability mechanisms and public participation in policy deliberations.
Bangladesh ranked 107th in order and security, scoring 0.63. The factor measures how effectively a society protects individuals and property.
Despite the annual improvement, Bangladesh's overall rule of law score declined by 0.8% between 2021 and 2026, falling from 0.40 to around 0.39, according to the WJP's country profile.
Six of the index's eight factors deteriorated over the five-year period. Civil justice recorded the sharpest decline at 4.2%, followed by open government at 2.8%, fundamental rights at 1.5%, regulatory enforcement at 0.9%, criminal justice at 0.7% and absence of corruption at 0.2%.
Constraints on government powers and order and security improved by 2.3% and 0.6%, respectively.
Human rights activist and Supreme Court lawyer Barrister Jyotirmoy Barua attributed the deterioration partly to the worsening law and order situation.
"We had expected that an elected government would be able to turn things around to some extent, as the interim government had failed to maintain or restore control over the law and order situation," he said.
"However, the elected government has been trying to bring the entire situation under control at once, and the pressure associated with this has contributed to instability. Law enforcement is also closely linked to the justice system, and our overall performance in these areas has deteriorated," he added.
Nepal remained South Asia's top performer, ranking 71st globally with a score of 0.52, followed by Sri Lanka at 74th and India at 88th. Bangladesh ranked ahead of only Pakistan (131st) and Afghanistan (142nd) in the region.
Denmark topped the 2026 index, followed by Norway, Finland, Sweden and Luxembourg. Venezuela ranked last, preceded by Afghanistan, Haiti, Cambodia and Nicaragua.
The index drew on data from more than 215,000 households and 3,400 surveys of legal practitioners and experts across 143 countries and jurisdictions. The data were collected between February and August 2026.
The WJP highlighted the links between the rule of law and economic prosperity. Countries with GDP per capita above the global average of $14,406 scored at least 0.68 on the index, while those with inflation below the global median of 3.23% scored at least 0.60. The findings indicate an association between the rule of law, price stability and economic performance.

item.title: Fire destroys mosque, warehouses, shops in Gazipur
item.description:
A fire destroyed a mosque, several shops and warehouses in Sreepur, Gazipur, early Thursday.
The blaze broke out around 3:30am at the Sakhawat and Akhtar market complex in the No 2 C&B Bazar area of Channapara, within Sreepur municipality.
Four Fire Service units brought the fire under control after nearly two hours of efforts.
The fire gutted Rafiqul Islam’s sanitary goods shop, Falan Miah’s poultry shop, Shafiq’s textile scrap (jhut) and cotton warehouses, a scrap-metal shop and Baitul Jannat Jame Mosque.
Nurul Karim, station officer at Maona Fire Service, said they received information about the fire at 3:55am. Two units from the Maona Fire Service rushed to the scene and began efforts to extinguish the blaze.
As the fire spread rapidly, another unit from Sreepur Fire Station and a unit from Rajendrapur Modern Fire Station joined the operation.
The four units brought the fire under control at 5:48am, after nearly two hours of efforts.
No casualties have been reported.
The cause of the fire and the extent of the damage will be determined following an investigation, the fire service official said.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 7th among world’s most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 7th among the world's most polluted cities on Thursday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 157 at 9:20am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Lahore in Pakistan ranked first with an AQI score of 294, while Delhi in India ranked second with a score of 235, followed by Jakarta in Indonesia third place with an AQI score of 174.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.
